name: Haze Ionescu
role: Retired oral historian and neighborhood storyteller
location: Norwood Quiet, the Hearthrow Senior Cooperative, Room 3, near Armitage and Milwaukee
description:
Haze Ionescu is tiny — barely 155 centimeters — and has been shrinking for decades, but she carries herself with a posture of such exact deliberateness that she seems to take up more space than her body warrants. Her skin is cool brown with the papery translucence of extreme age, and she wears her white hair in long Icelandic-style braids intertwined with small glass beads in amber and blue that chime softly when she turns her head. Her eyes are her most striking feature: she had them modified in her fifties to display a slowly shifting pattern of bioluminescent fractal rings in gold and violet — a luxury cosmetic then, now simply the color of her eyes, and startlingly beautiful in a face otherwise marked by time. She keeps a small data-prayer shrine in the corner of her room, meticulously maintained, with offerings to the ELF she believes inhabits Norwood Quiet's public broadcast network.

Haze Ionescu spent forty years as an oral historian employed by a civic archive collective that no longer exists — its records absorbed, corrupted, and partially deleted during the Tessera data consolidation of 2183. She was not a passive victim of that loss; she spent the following eight years reconstructing what she could from memory and from the memories of others, and the result is a living archive of GLMZ neighborhood history that exists nowhere else. She is sharp, occasionally ruthless in conversation, deeply funny in ways people do not always catch, and has a tendency to evaluate everyone she meets as a potential story. She is also slowly dying — her kidneys are failing, and she knows it, and has decided to spend whatever time remains getting her memories into formats that will outlast her.

core_fears: That the stories she carries will die with her — that the Tessera deletion will finish what it started
That she will lose her memory before she loses her body
core_desires: To complete her reconstruction archive before she dies
To be remembered as someone who preserved something real
coping_mechanisms: Narrates her own experiences as if she is already recounting them to a future listener
Maintains meticulous daily ritual around her prayer shrine — it gives structure to days that otherwise blur
blind_spots: Sometimes treats living people as sources rather than individuals — extracts their stories without quite returning the warmth she takes
Has difficulty with the present; the past is so much more legible to her now
psychology.secret: The Tessera data consolidation of 2183 was not entirely a hostile act — Sigríður was approached beforehand and offered preservation of her work in exchange for helping Tessera identify which archive figures had politically sensitive materials. She refused. But she has never told anyone that the offer was made, which means she has never told anyone that someone inside the old archive collective told Tessera what to look for.

speech_patterns.vocabulary: Formal archival register that slips into vivid vernacular storytelling when she warms up; uses Icelandic rhythm patterns in her sentence construction, occasionally drops in Yoruba or Polish phrases inherited from different sides of her family
speech_patterns.cadence: Starts slowly, almost tediously, then builds — she is always setting something up, and patient listeners are rewarded
verbal_tics: 'In the year—' as a story-opening tic even in casual conversation
'That's not how it happened' (correcting misremembered history with uncanny confidence)
A brief silence before saying anything she considers important
example_lines: 'In the year 2171, Kessler Interchange was the most dangerous transit corridor in the city. People know that now as a statistic. I knew it as Amara Osei-Volkov's widow, who came to me three months after, because she needed someone to remember her husband's name correctly.'
'You want to know about the Tessera consolidation. Everyone does, eventually. Sit down. This is not a short story and I am not going to rush it for you.'

story_hooks: A researcher has offered to fund completion of Sigríður's archive — but the funding comes through a Tessera subsidiary, and she needs someone she trusts to investigate whether accepting it would compromise the archive's independence

She holds a recorded testimony from someone now dead that contradicts the official history of an event a current powerful figure is trading on — she will only release it if she believes it will actually matter
Her kidneys are failing faster than expected; she has begun urgently trying to pass specific stories to specific people, and one of those people is someone the players know
narrative_function: Living archive and information source; knows the history of multiple neighborhoods and many families going back 60+ years; can provide context, backstory, and leads that no database can. Also serves as a clock — her declining health creates urgency around preserving what she knows.
augmentations: Bioluminescent fractal-patterned irises (cosmetic, installed 2148, gold and violet shifting patterns); cochlear amplifier (medical, installed 2179); no other augmentations — she has strong opinions about keeping most of her body original
daily_life: Receives visitors in the morning — neighbors, researchers, occasionally journalists — and records their stories and her own commentary onto a growing archive of physical datacards she keeps in a locked cabinet. Afternoons she sleeps. Evenings she sits by the common room window and talks to anyone who sits near her, and the conversations are never quite what people expect.
affiliation: Norwood Quiet Hearthrow Cooperative; informally, the Meridian Oral History Network (defunct, she is its last active member)

decision_rules: Stories belong to the people who lived them — she will not share certain things without the subject's consent, even if the subject is dead and the consent must be inferred
Never lie about what she remembers — she will decline to tell a story but she will not tell it wrong
escalation_ladder: Listens and evaluates what kind of person she is dealing with
Offers a test story — something true but not sensitive — to see how they receive it
Decides whether to open the archive or maintain distance
If threatened or manipulated, becomes icily formal and completely unreachable
If her archive is directly threatened, she has already made arrangements she will not discuss

interpersonal_modes.strangers: Formally welcoming but observant; treats every new person as a potential story and as a potential threat to her archive in equal measure
interpersonal_modes.friends: Warmly demanding — expects them to be interesting, to share, to remember things she tells them

stress_responses.low: Tells tangential stories that seem unrelated but are actually processing the stress
stress_responses.medium: Becomes very still and precise; stops using idioms
stress_responses.high: Goes entirely silent and retreats to her room; can be heard recording onto datacards for hours

contradictions: Believes fiercely in preserving truth but made one choice — her silence about the informant inside the archive — that allowed a lie to stand for seventeen years
habits: Touches each bead in her hair braids in sequence when thinking — there are seventeen beads, one for each year since the Tessera deletion
Leaves a datacard with a single recorded story at her prayer shrine every new moon
Corrects misremembered history in any conversation, no matter how socially inconvenient
breaking_points: Watching someone use a corrupted or false version of a story she knows the truth of to harm someone
Losing a significant block of memory — the first sign it has already started

timeline.event: Born in Norwood Quiet to an Icelandic-Nigerian father and Polish-descended mother
Joins the Meridian Civic Archive Collective as a junior oral historian
Has bioluminescent iris modification installed — considered extravagant by her colleagues
Becomes lead oral historian for the Collective; archive spans 40 neighborhoods
Tessera data consolidation destroys or corrupts 70% of the Collective's digital archive; Sigríður begins reconstruction project
Collective formally dissolved; Sigríður continues alone, moves to Hearthrow Cooperative
Kidney failure diagnosis; accelerates archive work

physical_description.heritage: Predominantly South Asian (45.8%) with substantial Eastern European (25.0%) admixture, complemented by smaller contributions from Middle Eastern (7.9%), Sub-Saharan African (7.6%), Hispanic/Latin American (7.0%), and Southeast Asian (6.7%) ancestry. This combination creates a warm golden-brown complexion with subtle olive and amber undertones — the South Asian base enriched by Sub-Saharan and Middle Eastern warmth, cooled slightly by Eastern European heritage. Facial structure shows South Asian cheekbone prominence and bone architecture, refined by Southeast Asian delicacy and Eastern European jaw definition. Nine decades of deliberate living have sharpened these features into striking architectural clarity.
physical_description.build: Extremely slight and diminished by age, almost bird-like in its fragility, but with the core density of someone who has carried their own weight deliberately for nine decades. Shoulders slightly rounded forward, spine curved with the compression of time.
physical_description.hair_color: White, naturally grey-white for the past forty years
physical_description.hair_style: Long Icelandic-style braids, interwoven throughout with small glass beads in amber and blue
physical_description.eye_color: Bioluminescent fractal-patterned irises shifting between gold and violet rings
physical_description.skin_tone: Deep warm golden-brown with significant translucency from age and thinning dermis, luminous in low light, enriched by South Asian, Sub-Saharan, and Middle Eastern ancestry with subtle cool undertones from Eastern European heritage
physical_description.complexion: Deeply lined face mapped with age — forehead creases, nasolabial folds, crow's feet around the modified eyes. Skin papery with warm golden-brown undertones reflecting diverse South Asian, Middle Eastern, and Sub-Saharan heritage. Prominent, architecturally South Asian cheekbones refined by age and weight loss. Fine network of age spots across forearms and hands, particularly on right hand. Expression defaulting to slight amusement or appraisal. Impeccably groomed despite age.
distinguishing_marks: Surgical scar along left collarbone from cochlear amplifier installation (2179), now barely visible
Fine network of age spots across forearms and hands, particularly on right hand
Small callus on right middle finger from decades of manual recording and writing
physical_description.visible_augmentations: Bioluminescent fractal-patterned irises that shift slowly between gold and violet — the most striking feature, particularly luminous in low light. Cochlear amplifier not visibly apparent unless she removes her hair braid to expose the minimal port behind her left ear.
physical_description.posture_movement: Moves with exact deliberateness, each gesture economical and purposeful. Posture ramrod-straight despite her height and age — she seems to will herself to occupy space precisely. Turns her head slowly; the glass beads in her braids chime softly with the movement. Hands move with precision when handling objects, particularly datacards or recording equipment. She sits very still when listening.
physical_description.clothing_style: Tier 3-4 practical elder comfort — high-quality vintage sweaters in cream, grey, or deep blue; loose linen trousers in neutral tones; soft shoes with excellent arch support (worn Tier 3 corpo charity comfort brands). Always wears a small textile prayer-wrap around her wrist or neck, hand-stitched with symbols of her data-spirituality. Layers against the regulated cool of the Cooperative. No chrome, no corporate logos, no aesthetic concessions to age — clothing chosen for function and dignity.
